narrator.instruct: Fast, gripping, high-energy history storyteller. Excited and urgent, punchy emphasis on the surprising facts, brisk pace, no long pauses.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: During World War Two, bombs crossed the Pacific without a pilot.

voice.instruct: Dramatic, excited opening hook, urgent and amazed, hitting 'without a pilot' hard.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Japan built about nine thousand three hundred paper balloons, glued by teenage schoolgirls.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Full of hydrogen, they rode the jet stream thirty-five thousand feet up, six thousand miles to America.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whenever one sank, it dropped a sandbag and climbed again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: About three hundred made it. Alaska, Montana, even Michigan.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: America told newspapers to print nothing. Japan was left guessing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Geologists studied the sand in those bags to hunt down the launch beaches.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then, on May fifth, nineteen forty-five, a church picnic in an Oregon forest found one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Six people died, the only deaths from enemy attack on the American mainland.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And some of those balloons were never found.
